What is UHC?

On this page

World Generation & Mutation Architecture Guide ​

This guide describes the modular architecture of the AetherUHC world generation and mutation systems. Following a major refactoring, these modules are designed to run both integrated (embedded inside the main AetherUHC game plugin) and standalone (as lightweight map-pregen plugins).

1. High-Level Architecture ​

The world generation system is split into multiple modules under a parent Maven project. This decoupling isolates heavyweight game logic, databases, and event listeners from the performance-critical chunk generation and block mutation logic.

Module Breakdown ​

ModuleTarget JavaDependenciesPurpose
WorldGenCoreJava 8Spigot API (1.8.8)Contains all platform-independent code, including the block mutation scheduler, chunk ticketing structures, Dragon Rush structures, and transform definitions (Big Crack, Chunk Apocalypse, etc.).
AetherMapLegacyJava 8Spigot API (1.8.8)Houses the synchronous, row-scanning LegacySquareFillEngine for legacy platforms.
AetherMapModernJava 21Paper API (1.20+)Houses high-performance asynchronous pregen engine (AsyncSquareFillEngine / ForceloadBatchPregenEngine) utilizing Paper's multi-threaded chunk loading.
AetherWorldGenJava 8WorldGenCore, AetherMapLegacyBase shell for the standalone plugins. Includes commands (/worldgen) and shared configuration loaders.
AetherWorldGenModernJava 21AetherWorldGen, AetherMapModernModern entrypoint bootstrap utilizing Paper's PluginBootstrap to inject datapacks at early startup.

2. Core Abstractions & Interfaces ​

To allow code inside WorldGenCore to execute inside the UHC plugin or the standalone shell without class-loading errors, all operations are decoupled using two interfaces:

WorldGenContext ​

Replaces direct static references to AetherUHC.getInstance(). It abstracts logging, scheduler dispatching, version detection, and message broadcasting:

java
public interface WorldGenContext {
    JavaPlugin getPlugin();
    Logger getLogger();
    WorldGenConfigProvider getConfigProvider();
    boolean isModernPlatform();
    boolean isOnePointEighteenPlus();
    void broadcastMessage(String message);
    void log(String message);
    void debug(String message);
}

WorldGenConfigProvider ​

Abstracts file access (e.g. worldmanagement.yml or uhcconfiguration.yml). This enables the core logic to read configuration entries regardless of whether they are hosted inside the standalone YAML parser or the main UHC configuration managers:

java
public interface WorldGenConfigProvider {
    boolean contains(String path);
    int getInt(String path, int defaultValue);
    boolean getBoolean(String path, boolean defaultValue);
    String getString(String path);
    java.util.List<String> getStringList(String path);
    void setString(String path, String value);
    void setStringList(String path, java.util.List<String> values);
    void save();
}

3. World Pre-Generation Subsystem ​

Map pre-generation ensures that all chunks within a game boundary are generated and saved to disk before players join, eliminating runtime generator lag.

A. Legacy Pregen (LegacySquareFillEngine) ​

  • Runs a synchronous loop on the Spigot primary thread.
  • Performs a linear row-scan over the map coordinate coordinates.
  • Throttling: Constrained by a strict timeBudgetMs (usually 95ms) and a maximum chunks-per-tick count. If the generation of a chunk exceeds the budget, execution halts until the next tick.
  • Memory Safety: Maintains a ring-buffer array of chunk coordinates. Chunks that were generated are queued and unloaded after moving out of the buffer, forcing Spigot to free memory.

B. Modern Pregen (AsyncSquareFillEngine) ​

  • Built specifically for modern Paper servers.
  • Uses Paper's async chunk loading APIs (world.getChunkAtAsyncUrgently()) to schedule chunk generation off-thread.
  • Active Thread Control: Uses a Semaphore to limit the number of active concurrent chunk tasks (e.g., 320 max) so as not to overwhelm the server's thread pools.
  • Memory Safety: Periodically flushes changes to disk and calls world.save() on a timer (SAVE-INTERVAL-SECONDS), then releases the async tickets to avoid Java Virtual Machine out-of-memory errors on massive borders.
  • Disk Validation: After completion, a coordinate-scanning loop checks world.isChunkGenerated() to ensure zero chunks were dropped.

4. Post-Generation Mutation Subsystem ​

Post-generation transformations apply custom rules directly to blocks (e.g., carving cracks, wiping layers, or mirroring levels). Because block manipulations are heavy, these are scheduled in a tick-budgeted, memory-safe runner.

How ChunkRegionRunner Works ​

  1. Coord Gathering: A transform defines a boundary. The runner calculates all chunks overlapping this boundary.
  2. Warmup Window: The runner loads chunks in a sliding window (e.g. 48 chunks ahead of the cursor) asynchronously using Paper's plugin ticket system (ChunkTicketScope).
  3. Execution: Once the chunk at the cursor reaches a fully generated state (LevelChunk), it is passed to the transform's block callback.
  4. MSPT-Aware Budgeting: Writes are governed by MutationBudget. It tracks how many blocks have been written in the current tick. If the server MSPT (Milliseconds Per Tick) exceeds a threshold (e.g., 50ms) or blocks-per-tick exceeds the limit (e.g., 12,000), it yields execution to the next tick.
  5. Direct Block Write: Uses direct Chunk#setBlockData which modifies the chunk storage memory without triggering block physics updates, avoiding massive cascading block updates.

5. No-Oceans Datapack Injection ​

On Minecraft 1.18+, custom generation properties (like replacing deep ocean biomes with plains or forests) are handled by Vanilla Minecraft datapacks.

[Server Bootstrap]
       │
       ▼
AetherWorldGenModernBootstrap (extends PaperPluginBootstrap)
       │
       ▼
NoOceansDatapack.inject()
       │
       ├── 1. Generate Virtual Datapack ZIP in memory / temp files
       ├── 2. Hook into BootstapContext Configuration
       └── 3. Inject "plain" biome mappings over "deep_ocean"
  1. Bootstrap Phase Hooking: The modern standalone module implements Paper's PluginBootstrap and registers itself in paper-plugin.yml.
  2. In-Memory Injection: NoOceansDatapack.java dynamically generates a zip file containing the biome configuration adjustments (e.g., swapping minecraft:ocean and minecraft:deep_ocean noise parameters to continental land-forms).
  3. Vanilla Registration: The bootstrap code injects this datapack directly into Paper's datapack resource manager before the world generator initializes, ensuring the map generates oceanless.

6. How to Extend: Adding a Custom Transform ​

To create a new world mutation/post-gen effect, follow these steps:

Step 1: Create the Transform Class ​

In WorldGenCore, create a class extending AbstractPostWorldGenTransform:

java
package net.aetheruhc.worldgen.postgen;

import net.aetheruhc.worldgen.WorldGenContext;
import org.bukkit.Chunk;
import org.bukkit.World;

public class MyCustomTransform extends AbstractPostWorldGenTransform {

    public MyCustomTransform() {
        super(PostWorldGenTransformId.MY_CUSTOM, "My Custom Transform");
    }

    @Override
    protected void transformChunk(WorldGenContext context, World world, Chunk chunk, PostWorldGenParams params) {
        // This is called for every chunk inside the boundary.
        // Implement your block manipulation here!
        
        int minX = chunk.getX() << 4;
        int minZ = chunk.getZ() << 4;
        
        for (int x = 0; x < 16; x++) {
            for (int z = 0; z < 16; z++) {
                // Keep performance in mind; check budget limits if doing massive operations
                int worldX = minX + x;
                int worldZ = minZ + z;
                
                // Write blocks using chunk-local editors
                // e.g. chunk.getBlock(x, 64, z).setType(Material.STONE);
            }
        }
    }
}

Step 2: Register the Transform ID ​

In PostWorldGenTransformId.java (under net.aetheruhc.worldgen.postgen), add your transform:

java
public enum PostWorldGenTransformId {
    BIG_CRACK,
    CHUNK_APOCALYPSE,
    UNDERGROUND_PARALLEL,
    DRAGON_RUSH,
    MY_CUSTOM; // Add here!
    
    public static PostWorldGenTransformId fromString(String name) {
        try {
            return valueOf(name.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT));
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
            return null;
        }
    }
}

Step 3: Register in the Registry ​

In PostWorldGenRegistry.java, register your implementation:

java
public class PostWorldGenRegistry {
    public PostWorldGenRegistry() {
        register(new BigCrackTransform());
        register(new ChunkApocalypseTransform());
        register(new UndergroundParallelTransform());
        register(new DragonRushTransform());
        register(new MyCustomTransform()); // Register here!
    }
    // ...
}

7. Developer Compilation Commands ​

Use standard Maven commands from the repository root:

  • Build everything:
    bash
    mvn clean package
  • Build WorldGenCore only (fast testing):
    bash
    mvn package -pl WorldGenCore

Output binaries will be populated inside the Base/release/ directory:

  • AetherWorldGen.jar (Java 21 standalone plugin for Paper 1.20+)
  • AetherWorldGen-Legacy.jar (Java 8 standalone plugin for 1.8 Spigot)
  • AetherUHC.jar (Modern full integrated UHC plugin)
  • AetherUHC-Legacy.jar (Legacy full integrated UHC plugin)
